item.title: Trump vows to release classified information on aliens after admonishing Obama for commenting on classified information about aliens
item.description: Trump has a lengthy history of retaining classified information. He said he would “help“ Obama by declassifying any documents related to aliens or UFOs.

item.description: But sadly, the economic uncertainty isn't over.

item.title: ‘We are in a dismal fiscal situation, and it just got worse’: Budget watchdog sounds the alarm even louder after Supreme Court erases Trump’s tariffs
item.description: Many shoppers and companies might cheer the drawdown of Trump’s tariffs, but the truth is America really needed that money.

item.title: Trump calls Supreme Court justices who struck down his tariffs a ‘disgrace to our nation’ and vows fresh duties under other laws
item.description: “I’m ashamed of certain members of the court, absolutely ashamed for not having the courage to do what’s right for our country,” Trump told reporters.

item.title: Trump warns he’s considering limited strikes on Iran and says Tehran ‘better negotiate a fair deal’
item.description: Ali Vaez, an Iran expert at the International Crisis Group, said Iran “would treat any kinetic action as an existential threat.”

item.title: Trump imposes 10% global tariff in bid to salvage trade plans
item.description: Along with the flat 10% rate, Trump said he would keep in place existing import taxes under Section 301 and Section 232 and signaled plans to launch more trade investigations.

item.title: OpenAI forecasts its revenue will top $280 billion in 2030
item.description: OpenAI Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar recently said the company’s annualized revenue topped $20 billion in 2025, up from roughly $6 billion the year prior.

item.title: Detroit automakers ask White House to be spared from new tariffs
item.description: The American Automotive Policy Council, which represents GM, Ford and Jeep-maker Stellantis, sent a letter to Trump’s trade team on Friday.

item.title: Trump loves cheap gas—but a military conflict in Iran could nearly double your price at the pump
item.description: As Trump builds the biggest military force since 2003 outside Iran, the U.S. impacts could swing from $2.50 to $5 gasoline.
